newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Two dead, 46 hurt in South African blasts.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, 46 hurt in South African blasts.

text.p: Three explosions went off in a small South African farming town on Tuesday, one at a supermarket crowded with Christmas Eve shoppers, and police said at least two people were killed and 46 hurt.
Spokesman Wicus Holtzhausen told Reuters two explosions went off at a chemist shop in Worcester, 90 km (56 miles) northeast of Cape Town, and one at a crowded supermarket.
He said it was not known what caused the explosions at about 2.30 p.m. (1230 GMT), but a doctor at the town's hospital said he believed they had been bombs.
Dr Frans Krige said he had heard one of the explosions, which sounded like a cannon going off.
"We have had about 30 casualties admitted here and more were taken to a private clinic. One of the casualties here died and four others were seriously hurt," Krige said.
"The bombs have caused a huge commotion here. No one can understand why anyone would want to plant bombs here."
Worcester is a small town surrounded by picturesque mountains in a fruit-growing district.
